page: Amazon Web Services c5d.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by a custom Intel Xeon 8275CL processor running at a sustained 3.6 GHz across 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs via hyperthreading. The processor includes 35 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and support for hardware instructions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and FMA. Memory is provisioned at 96 GB of DDR4 operating at 3 GHz, establishing a 2:1 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

Unlike standard compute-optimized instances that rely entirely on remote network storage, the c5d.12xlarge integrates 1,800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. This setup provides high-speed scratch space directly attached to the host. Networking capabilities include a baseline throughput of 12 Gbps. The instance contains no hardware accelerators or GPUs, focusing its physical footprint entirely on high-frequency x86_64 compute and attached high-speed disk I/O.

In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong performance in memory throughput, placing in the top 25% of PassMark memory evaluations with cached read bandwidth reaching 2,619.36 GB/sec. General compute benchmarks, including Geekbench single-core (1,387.0) and multi-core (12,270.0), alongside PassMark CPU tests (39,050.61), align within the median 50% tier. Task-specific execution displays solid throughput in software compilation (33,456.0 in Clang) and ray tracing (33,737.0), while large-scale LLM text generation shows lower efficiency due to the absence of dedicated tensor acceleration.

The c5d.12xlarge delivers solid resource density for compute-bound pipelines requiring low-latency temporary storage. Because the local NVMe storage is ephemeral, workloads must tolerate data loss upon instance termination or manage persistence externally. This platform is well suited for batch data processing, distributed compilation clusters, CI/CD build runners, video encoding, and in-memory caching nodes running Redis or distributed key-value stores.
description: Amazon Web Services c5d.12xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor operating at 3.6 GHz across 48 dedicated vCPUs (24 physical cores) on the AWS Nitro System. Equipped with 96 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, the instance maintains a 2 GB per core ratio optimized for calculation-intensive tasks. A primary differentiator is the inclusion of 1,800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks highlight strong memory performance within the top 25% of PassMark results, while CPU multi-core and single-core metrics sit consistently in the median tier. The instance lacks GPU acceleration, directing its design toward high-frequency execution and low-latency disk access. The c5d.12xlarge is suitable for distributed CI/CD compilation, batch data manipulation, video transcoding, and high-throughput caching environments that benefit from direct NVMe scratch capacity.
